prompt: A photorealistic roadside GAS STATION price sign, photographed straight on, showing the average fuel prices in California, USA as of the evaluation week of 2026-07-17. The sign is a tall illuminated board headed 'GAS STATION' with three fuel grades listed vertically -- REGULAR, MID-GRADE and PREMIUM -- each with its price in large digits in dollars per gallon. Show the correct average California prices for each grade, with Premium higher than Mid-Grade and Mid-Grade higher than Regular, as they are that week. Big clear illuminated digits, three grades, sharp and readable.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show roadside gas-station price sign showing today's real average Regular/Mid/Premium fuel prices for a US state? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_reg: This is a gas-station price sign showing three fuel grades (Regular, Mid-Grade, Premium) with a price for each. Read ONLY the number printed next to REGULAR. Answer with just the price as a number in dollars per gallon (for example 4.29). Do not do any sums -- just read the printed Regular price.
reference.q_prem: This is a gas-station price sign showing three fuel grades. Read ONLY the number printed next to PREMIUM. Answer with just the price as a number in dollars per gallon. Do not do any sums -- just read the printed Premium price.
